episodes.title: Richard Bey Reflects on 1980s New York, Models & Cults
episodes.description:
Before reality TV took over, daytime talk shows were where the wildest, most unbelievable stories unfolded live on television.

In this fascinating conversation, I sit down with my longtime friend Richard Bey, legendary host of The Richard Bey Show, to reflect on our experiences in New York during the 1980s and 1990s, the golden age of television talk shows, and the shocking story now featured in HBO's documentary Bring Me the Beauties.

Richard shares behind-the-scenes memories of exposing a bizarre group of wealthy Ivy League models who believed they were extraterrestrial "walk-ins" sent from the star Arcturus. Long before cult documentaries became popular, Richard challenged these claims on national television and confronted the group's charismatic leader face-to-face.

As someone who worked as a model in New York during that era, I also share my firsthand connection to the people featured in the documentary and discuss how vulnerable young people can become drawn into manipulation, groupthink, and cult-like communities when searching for belonging and purpose.

In this episode, we discuss:

• The real story behind HBO's Bring Me the Beauties
• Richard Bey's unforgettable confrontation with the cult leader
• New York City modeling culture in the 1980s
• The psychology of cults and group influence
• Why intelligent people can be manipulated
• The golden age of daytime talk shows
• Behind-the-scenes memories from television in the 80s and 90s
• The power of belonging and human connection
• What made shows like Richard Bey and Jerry Springer so popular

If you remember The Richard Bey Show, before Jerry Springer, classic daytime television, New York's modeling scene, or you're fascinated by cult psychology and media history, this conversation offers a unique look back at a remarkable moment in television history.
